issues.title: Levels 5–9 can resolve OPPOSITE into a direction that is not active for the level
issues.issue: Dynamic OPPOSITE targeting transforms the previous direction by compass opposite without revalidating the result against the level's active directions.
issues.whyThisIsBug: Levels 5–9 explicitly restrict which fronts are active. OPPOSITE is applied after that level-domain selection but its result is not checked against the same active-direction list, so the runtime can use a front that the current level configuration did not enable.
issues.impact: Players can be attacked from South before South is introduced by the level progression. Defensive positioning, block placement, team coverage, and encounter difficulty can therefore differ from the authored Level 5–9 front layout.
reproduction: Start Defense Challenge on Level 5, 6, 7, 8, or 9 with the declared active fronts visible for that level.
Reach a wave entry that uses OPPOSITE after the previous dynamic target resolves to North.
Observe which logical spawn route is selected for the OPPOSITE entry.
Confirm whether South is selected even though South is not declared active until Level 10.
issues.observed: Levels 5–6 declare north/east and Levels 7–9 declare north/east/west, but OPPOSITE(north) resolves south; South routes are configured and materialized even though South is not active until Level 10.
issues.expected: Every resolved spawn direction remains inside the current level's declared direction domain.
issues.resolution: Validate every transformed direction against levelConfig.directions and choose a deterministic valid fallback when the opposite front is inactive.
issues.technicalAnalysis: The resulting South target is routable; no post-transform domain guard was found.

relevantCode.reason: Levels 5–9 restricted direction sets and OPPOSITE entries.

mustPreserve: South dual-route behavior from Level 10 onward

issues.title: Reload does not faithfully restore deferred wave timing and delayed spawn groups
issues.issue: Persisted session state records launched-wave progress but does not fully persist/reconstruct remaining inter-wave and intra-wave deferred work.
issues.whyThisIsBug: A persisted active session must resume the same outstanding encounter work, not merely remember which wave index was last launched. The current recovery state cannot reconstruct remaining delays or delayed sub-groups, so reload changes the encounter that was in progress.
issues.impact: After reload, a pending wave can arrive at the wrong time, and Level 15 can permanently omit the delayed East/West group of six NPCs. This changes combat pressure and can make the resumed run easier or structurally different from the pre-reload run.
reproduction: Start a level with a pending delayed wave or delayed spawn group and note the remaining delay.
Reload or recover the persisted Defense session before the pending delay expires.
Observe the timing and composition of the next resumed wave or group.
For Level 15 Wave 3, reload during the 10-second delay before the East/West six-NPC group and confirm whether that delayed group is reconstructed.
issues.observed: Recovery resumes from lastLaunchedWaveIndex without using currentWaveElapsedTicks as remaining-delay authority. Level 15 Wave 3 is marked launched before its +10-second East/West group of six NPCs materializes, so reload in that window can lose the in-memory delayed group.
issues.expected: Reload preserves the same pending timing and delayed spawn groups that existed immediately before reload.
issues.resolution: Persist a reconstructable pending-wave timeline including remaining delays for intra-wave delayed groups.
issues.technicalAnalysis: Wave-index persistence is not sufficient to reconstruct all scheduled work.

issues.title: Configured captureZone is not the authoritative flag-capture boundary
issues.issue: Arena configuration describes captureZone as hostile flag detection, while FlagService uses it for warning coverage and a separate hard-coded radius for defeat.
issues.whyThisIsBug: The arena configuration presents captureZone as the flag-detection boundary, but runtime defeat is decided by a separate hard-coded 1.3 horizontal / 1.5 vertical radius. Two different authorities therefore describe the same objective boundary.
issues.impact: Warning and defeat behavior can be reasoned about from different spatial rules. Designers and developers can tune captureZone without changing the actual defeat trigger, creating misleading configuration and making flag-balance changes unreliable.
reproduction: Run a Defense level with a hostile approaching the configured flag captureZone.
Observe the hostile while it is inside the configured captureZone but outside the hard-coded 1.3-block horizontal defeat radius.
Confirm whether warning state and defeat state use different boundaries.
Repeat near the 1.3-block boundary to identify the actual defeat trigger.
issues.observed: captureZone is configured/offset per arena, but actual defeat uses horizontal radius 1.3 and vertical radius 1.5.
issues.expected: Warning and defeat boundaries have one explicit non-conflicting authority whose naming matches runtime behavior.
issues.resolution: Choose one capture authority and rename/separate warning configuration if the hard-coded defeat radius is canonical.
issues.technicalAnalysis: This is an internal authority mismatch, not a claim that 1.3 itself is the wrong gameplay value.

relevantCode.reason: Warning-zone derivation and hard-coded defeat radius.

issues.title: Shears special enemy resolves to ordinary Tier 2 behavior with no special-behavior consumer
issues.issue: The manifest defines SHEARS as a distinct gameplay type, but runtime maps it to Tier 2 militia and only adds shears_carrier.
issues.whyThisIsBug: SHEARS is authored as a distinct enemy type in the Defense wave manifest, but its only runtime distinction is a shears_carrier tag that nothing in the selected artifact consumes. A named special enemy therefore has no implemented behavior that makes the special type meaningful.
issues.impact: A wave that is configured to introduce a Shears-specific threat behaves like an ordinary Tier 2 militia encounter. Players do not receive the intended mechanical variation, and level difficulty/composition no longer matches the authored special-enemy identity.
reproduction: Reach a level that spawns the SHEARS special enemy.
Place the same valid defensive obstruction in the Shears path and in an ordinary Tier 2 militia path.
Compare the Shears enemy block interaction and combat behavior with ordinary Tier 2 militia.
Confirm whether any distinct Shears behavior is observable.
issues.observed: Across the selected artifact, shears_carrier appears only where the tag is added; no script, entity, controller, or behavior consumer reads it.
issues.expected: A distinct SHEARS gameplay type has an authoritative behavior consumer differentiating it from ordinary Tier 2 militia.
issues.resolution: Give SHEARS one explicit behavior owner or remove the distinct type if ordinary Tier 2 behavior is intended.
issues.technicalAnalysis: The special identity survives as metadata but not as behavior.

relevantCode.reason: SHEARS materialization and sole shears_carrier occurrence.

issues.title: Defense does not implement the approved crafting-UI disablement
issues.issue: Approved Defense design requires crafting UI unavailable during gameplay, but no crafting-screen UI override or equivalent owner exists.
issues.whyThisIsBug: The approved Defense requirement is to disable the crafting UI itself during gameplay. The selected artifact only changes specific recipes and does not remove or disable the crafting interface, so the implemented behavior does not satisfy the approved UI rule.
issues.impact: Players can still access a gameplay surface that is supposed to be unavailable. This makes the interaction rules inconsistent and leaves crafting visible even when individual recipes have been restricted.
reproduction: Start Defense Challenge and enter normal gameplay with inventory access.
Open the inventory and crafting interface.
Confirm whether the crafting UI remains available.
Verify that intended inventory, kit, and shop surfaces remain otherwise usable.
issues.observed: Selected RP contains HUD/information UI only. BP recipe overrides for stick/crafting table are not UI-level disablement.
issues.expected: Crafting UI is unavailable throughout Defense gameplay while intended inventory, kit and shop interactions remain available.
issues.resolution: Implement one explicit Defense crafting-availability owner at UI/capability level.
issues.technicalAnalysis: Current approved Defense requirement is not implemented in the selected artifact.

relevantCode.reason: Recipe overrides do not disable crafting UI.

issues.title: Defense result records identify v1.1.3 as v1.1.0
issues.issue: Machine-readable level/run record IDs use stale release provenance.
issues.whyThisIsBug: The selected world, behavior pack, and resource pack are v1.1.3, but persisted Defense result IDs still identify the run as v1.1.0. Result provenance therefore does not match the artifact that produced it.
issues.impact: Automated analysis, debugging, comparison, and historical result tracking can attribute v1.1.3 gameplay data to the wrong release. This weakens version traceability and can cause results from different builds to be grouped incorrectly.
reproduction: Complete or terminate a Defense run so level and run result records are persisted.
Inspect the generated Defense level and run record IDs.
Compare the version segment in those IDs with the selected world, BP, and RP version 1.1.3.
Confirm whether persisted record provenance still reports 1.1.0.
issues.observed: DEFENSE_RECORD_VERSION is hard-coded to 1.1.0 and embedded in level and run record IDs.
issues.expected: World/pack metadata and result persistence consume one canonical version and report 1.1.3.
issues.resolution: Consume one canonical release/version owner for persisted result provenance.
issues.technicalAnalysis: Selected world/BP/RP are v1.1.3 while score persistence carries the older literal.

issues.title: Retry configuration declares full-level restart while runtime uses remaining-NPC checkpoint recovery
issues.issue: marathonConfig.retryMode is full_level_restart, but it is not consumed as a behavior branch; retryLevel() preserves killed NPC IDs and resumes from the first incomplete wave.
issues.whyThisIsBug: The canonical configuration declares full_level_restart, while the actual retry implementation preserves killed NPCs and resumes remaining encounter state. The declared mode is not the behavior the game executes.
issues.impact: Developers reading or changing retryMode can reasonably expect a full restart but receive checkpoint-style recovery instead. Future balancing, fixes, or tooling can make incorrect decisions because configuration and runtime semantics disagree.
reproduction: Start a Defense level and defeat only part of the configured NPC population.
Trigger a level failure that enters retry.
Observe which enemies and wave state are restored for the retry.
Confirm that already-killed configured NPCs remain preserved and retry resumes remaining NPCs rather than performing a full-level restart.
issues.observed: retryMode is effectively logging metadata while remaining-NPC checkpoint behavior is hard-coded.
issues.expected: Declared retry mode and implemented retry behavior describe the same policy.
issues.resolution: Make remaining_npc_checkpoint canonical and consumed, or remove the unused mode abstraction.
issues.technicalAnalysis: The runtime checkpoint path is coherent; the mismatch is stale configuration.

devNotes.title: Partial Reset Results Are Recorded but Not Enforced Before Arena Reuse
devNotes.problem: ResetMapService can resolve with skippedChunks after a coverage recovery failure, while reuse consumers do not reject reuse solely because skippedChunks is non-empty.
devNotes.action: Retry or resolve skipped chunks before cleanup completes, or surface a hard reset failure that blocks reuse.

evidence.finding: processChunksOverTime() records skippedChunks and resolves; reuse does not inspect skippedChunks.

devNotes.title: Kit Selection Immediately Reapplies Loadout Without an Explicit Gameplay-Phase Gate
devNotes.problem: setSelectedKit() persists the selection, clears effects and immediately reapplies loadout without an explicit session-phase authorization check. Current source does not establish that combat-time kit changes are forbidden by Defense design.
devNotes.action: Define one authoritative kit-change policy; if preparation-only, enforce it at effect commit.

evidence.finding: setSelectedKit() has no GameManager phase check and immediately calls applySelectedKitNow().

devNotes.title: Several World-Mutating Script Events Do Not Use the Existing Developer Permission Owner
devNotes.problem: Several reset/force mutation handlers do not call PermissionService.canUseDeveloperTools(), while skip_level does. Ordinary-player command reachability is not claimed.
devNotes.action: Route every developer/admin world or session mutation through one explicit PermissionService gate.

evidence.finding: reset/force handlers and reset-map event lack the same internal permission owner used by skip_level.

devNotes.title: Admin Grant Secret Is Embedded in the Production Behavior Script
devNotes.problem: Permission configuration contains a literal admin grant/revoke secret in the distributed production BP.
devNotes.action: Use host/operator-controlled authorization rather than a static secret recoverable from the distributed pack.

evidence.finding: permissionConfig contains a literal secretCode used by PermissionService.

devNotes.title: Dedicated Persistent-Shop Preservation Helper Is Unused
devNotes.problem: A dedicated persistent-shop capture helper exists but the current loadout path relies on generic non-kit preservation instead.
devNotes.action: Remove the dead helper/option contract or connect one clear preservation owner.

evidence.finding: Persistent-shop-specific helper is defined without a production caller.

devNotes.title: Command-Delivered Shop Purchase Is Not Atomic
devNotes.problem: For giveCommand items, coins and purchase telemetry are committed before command delivery succeeds; failure has no rollback. Current source does not prove the configured Speed Potion command fails.
devNotes.action: Commit charge/telemetry after delivery succeeds, or refund/rollback on failure.

evidence.finding: _executePurchase() consumes coins and notifies purchase before awaiting giveCommand; catch path does not refund.

devNotes.title: Block-Break Scheduling Budget Is Shared Across All Six Arenas
devNotes.problem: BlockBreakService scans arenas in fixed order with global concurrency/start counters. Source proves coupling but not starvation or objective corruption.
devNotes.action: Use per-arena budgets or fair rotation if independent timing is required.

evidence.finding: scanAllArenas() uses one global start counter and one global breakStates cap across arena_1 through arena_6.

devNotes.title: CombatTracker Team-Wipe Comment Contradicts the Implemented Defense Outcome
devNotes.problem: A source comment says Defense wipes do not end the game, while GameManager routes team_wipe into level defeat/retry. The implemented path is treated as current behavior.
devNotes.action: Update or remove the stale comment.

evidence.finding: CombatTracker comment and GameManager team-wipe consumer describe different outcomes.

devNotes.title: Level 15 Completion-Coin Entry Is Unreachable
devNotes.problem: LEVEL_COMPLETION_COINS contains a 25-coin Level 15 entry, but completion coins are awarded only when a next level exists. Current source does not establish that final victory must award those coins.
devNotes.action: Remove the dead Level 15 entry or explicitly award it on final victory if intended.

evidence.finding: Level 15 goes directly to victory; awardLevelCompletionCoins() is called only on the next-level branch.
